title: Prime membership for a finite free module after localization
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $F=R^{n}$ a finite free $R$-module, $s=(s_1,\dots,s_n)\in F$, and $\mathfrak p\subset R$ a prime ideal. Put $S=R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and $F_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], with canonical map $F\to F_{\mathfrak p}$; write $R_{\mathfrak p}=S^{-1}R$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $s/1\in\mathfrak pF_{\mathfrak p}$ if and only if $s\in\mathfrak pF$. Equivalently, for each coordinate, $s_i/1\in\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ if and only if $s_i\in\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Algebra, Definition Tag 00CO and the localization-at-a-prime construction; the coordinate calculation underlying Lemma Tag 00NX (lemma-finite-projective)

proof.text: Membership in p times R^n is coordinatewise membership in p: induct on ideal scalar products for necessity, and write the vector as the finite sum of its coordinate multiples of standard coordinate vectors for sufficiency. Mathlib Submodule.localized'_smul, Ideal.localized'_eq_map and Submodule.localized'_top identify pF_p with the localization of pF [def-weil-pbc-module-localization, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. A fraction v/t with v in pF equal to s/1 supplies another denominator a with (at) • s = a • v. Thus each (at)s_i lies in p; because at is outside p, primality implies s_i in p. Conversely take v=s and t=1. For the scalar clause, IsLocalization.algebraMap_mem_map_algebraMap_iff supplies u outside p with us_i in p; primality gives s_i in p, and the converse uses u=1.

lean.statement: theorem free_prime_mem_localized_iff {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (n : ℕ) (s : Fin n → R) (p : Ideal R) [p.IsPrime] : (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap p.primeCompl (Fin n → R) s ∈ (Ideal.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p)) p) • (⊤ : Submodule (Localization.AtPrime p) (LocalizedModule p.primeCompl (Fin n → R))) ↔ s ∈ p • (⊤ : Submodule R (Fin n → R))) ∧ (∀ i : Fin n, algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p) (s i) ∈ Ideal.map (algebraMap R (Localization.AtPrime p)) p ↔ s i ∈ p)
